text:
Roles during application delivery

Role | Primary responsibilities
AI agents | Analyze requirements and code, suggest designs, generate or modify code and tests, assist with documentation, and help diagnose defects. Their output requires appropriate human review, testing, security controls, and approval.
Developers | Translate requirements and designs into working software, integrate services, write automated tests, review code, resolve defects, and support deployment and operations.
Architects | Define the technical direction, system boundaries, data and integration patterns, quality attributes, security approach, and major technology decisions.
Testers | Design and perform functional and nonfunctional testing, automate checks, investigate failures, report risks, and provide evidence about release readiness.
Product owners | Set product goals, prioritize the backlog, clarify requirements and acceptance criteria, balance stakeholder needs, and accept delivered outcomes.
Business users | Explain real workflows and constraints, validate needs and usability, participate in acceptance testing, provide feedback, and confirm that the application delivers business value.

These roles collaborate throughout delivery rather than working only in separate stages. Humans remain accountable for business priorities, architectural decisions, risk acceptance, and release approval; AI agents accelerate work but do not replace that accountability.
